mappings.note: pairs leaders with the vehicles they built (Bardoli, HSRA, Swaraj Party, Oudh Kisan Sabha) -- LO-2 covers 'other leaders' strategies', not LO-1's collective belonging; C-1.1 because the demand is bare pair recall
Bengal Gazette / Gangadhar Bhattacharya is Print Culture (ch 23709) content, not this chapter -- no LO here covers the early press, so the honest tag is the recall competency alone
Chauri Chaura as the reason for withdrawal is a judgement on Gandhiji's own strategy of non-violence, so LO-2; LO-3 stops at what triggered the movement, not what ended it
Vande Mataram is one of the icons LO-1 names as forging collective belonging; C-1.1 because the question asks only who wrote it
three of the four events (Champaran, Simon boycott, Purna Swaraj) are Congress/Gandhian moves, so LO-2 over LO-3; C-1.1 because only date order is tested
Punjab Kesri belongs to the press chapter, not this one (and the keyed answer is wrong -- Punjab Kesari was Lala Lajpat Rai's, Kesari was Tilak's); no LO covers it
the 1913 South Africa march is where the satyagraha technique was formed, so LO-2 rather than LO-1's Indian icons; C-1.1 because the task is identifying a photograph
all four events are leaders' acts and negotiations of 1930-32 (arrest, Gandhi-Irwin Pact, Bhagat Singh's execution, Poona Pact), so LO-2; C-1.1 for the date ordering
Sambad Kaumudi and Rammohan Roy are Print Culture (ch 23709) facts; nothing in this chapter's three outcomes reaches the nineteenth-century press
Kheda 1917 is one of the local trials of the satyagraha technique, so LO-2; it is not a Non-Cooperation trigger (LO-3) and not about a group's sense of nationhood (LO-1)
the sequence is built from Gandhiji's own milestones (return, Champaran, Dandi) with Khilafat as one item, so LO-2 carries it; C-1.1 for the ordering demand

the photograph is read for who was in the procession -- women entering nationalist politics in numbers is exactly LO-1's 'various facets ... collective belonging', not a judgement on Gandhiji's method
rich peasants' enthusiasm and their disappointment at the 1931 withdrawal is one social group's stake in the movement (LO-1); LO-2 would be the right code only if the pact itself were being judged
council entry is the alternative strategy C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru chose after Non-Cooperation -- 'other leaders' under LO-2, not a facet of mass belonging
RBI, Japan's industrialisation, Henry Ford and secularism belong to Economics, ch 23708 and Political Science -- nothing in this item is Nationalism in India; recall competency only
the pair asks whether repression explains the Gandhi-Irwin Pact, i.e. why the strategy turned to negotiation -- LO-2, not LO-1's participation
all three events are Gandhiji's own moves in the salt campaign (letter, law-breaking, pact), so LO-2; C-1.1 because only their order is asked
counting seats in a photograph to name Subhas Bose tests picture recall and nothing in any of the three outcomes; no LO is honestly available
the clues define satyagraha as a method (soul force, not seeking the opponent's destruction), which is the technique LO-2 asks to be evaluated
the four events are Gandhiji's arrival and his three satyagrahas, squarely LO-2; C-1.1 because the question is pure chronology
the table fixes the Dandi March dates and the salt monopoly it targeted -- the strategy's design (LO-2); C-1.1 because the cells wanted are a date and a target
Jallianwala Bagh is part of the post-war repression LO-3 names as the trigger of Khilafat and Non-Cooperation; it is not about method (LO-2)
Quit India (1942) and the Muslim League's founding (1906) fall outside this chapter entirely; a date list spanning 1906-1942 probes no one outcome
LO-3 names the Khilafat movement by name as the thing the war's aftermath triggered; the clues here are its cause and its Calcutta adoption, not Gandhiji's method
three of the four items (Chauri Chaura, Civil Disobedience, Second Round Table Conference) are stages of Congress strategy, so LO-2 over LO-3; C-1.1 for the ordering
